issues.location: Blueprint v1.md: multiple locations cite '7 of 36 agents touched' / '29 non-consumer agents preserve C-0445'. Specific lines: 53, 55, 95, 101, 154, 173, 206, 257 (AC-CC-3), 367 (Fact Disposition), 438, 451, 487 (Architecture Overview ASCII), 586 (Component #2), 687 (State Invariants), 968 (Implementation Plan step 7). Then Sub-Agents subsection line 749 says '7 of 36' followed by line 763 explicit resolution: 'Total touched agents: 8 ... The 28 untouched agents (36 − 8) preserve C-0445.'
issues.description: The Blueprint contains a load-bearing internal contradiction on agent counts. ADR-0040's Serena narrowing adds Serena entries to 5 agents (review-architecture-auditor, design-cc, design-cicd, design-codespaces, discovery-codebase-researcher). Three of those five (review-architecture-auditor, discovery-codebase-researcher, design-cicd) are already in the original 7-agent consumer-mapping; two (design-cc, design-codespaces) are new. The union of the consumer-mapping (7) and the Serena allowlist (5) is 8 unique touched agents; 36 − 8 = 28 untouched. ADR-0040 itself confirms this by stating '31 of 36 agents do not get mcp__serena__*' (which is consistent with 5 Serena consumers) and the Sub-Agents subsection explicitly resolves to 8/28. But every OTHER section of the Blueprint still cites the pre-narrowing figure of 7/29. AC-CC-3 in particular is operationally wrong: it states 'the operator inspects 29 non-consumer agent files' — but after this feature ships, only 28 files have zero mcp__ entries. A grep-based audit (which AC-CC-3 implicitly authorizes) will report a count mismatch.
issues.suggestion: Propagate the 8/28 figures consistently across the Blueprint. Specific edits: (1) AC-CC-3: change '29 non-consumer agent files' to '28 non-consumer agent files'. (2) Design Summary blast_radius.runtime: change '7 agents gain new mcp__ tool entries; the 29 untouched agents' to '8 agents gain new mcp__ tool entries; the 28 untouched agents'. (3) Design Summary main_constraints: change '29 non-consumer agents' to '28 non-consumer agents'. (4) Agreement Checklist Scope: change '7 of 36' to '8 of 36'. (5) Agreement Checklist Non-Scope: change 'C-0445 invariant for the 29 non-consumer agents' to '28 non-consumer agents'. (6) Fact Disposition Table row C-0445: change 'preserve (for 29 of 36)' to 'preserve (for 28 of 36)' and 'ADR-0040 narrows Serena' rationale should note '8 consumer agents total (3 from base mapping overlap with Serena consumers)'. (7) Change Impact Map No Ripple Effect: '29 non-consumer agents' → '28 non-consumer agents'. (8) Interface Change Matrix row: '7 of 36 agents gain ... 29 preserved' → '8 of 36 agents gain ... 28 preserved'. (9) Architecture Overview ASCII art line '(29 agents preserved zero-mcp__)' → '(28 agents preserved zero-mcp__)'. (10) Component #2 description: 'Preserve zero-mcp__ for 29 non-consumers' → '28 non-consumers'. (11) State Invariants: '29 of 36 agents always have zero mcp__ entries' → '28 of 36'. (12) Sub-Agents intro line 749: 'It modifies 7 of 36 existing agents' → '8 of 36'. (13) Implementation Plan step 7 line 968: '7 of 36 .claude/agents/*.md edits' → '8 of 36'. Plan-author depends on these counts being correct because the augmented auditing-mcp OP-3 rule (zero-mcp__ preservation) iterates over 28, not 29, files; a 29-cited count would cause an off-by-one audit-finding or, worse, the audit would silently treat the wrong file as a consumer.

issues.description: ADR-0037 Implementation Guidance contains a record-count value that contradicts the Blueprint's AC-X-2 inventory reconciliation. AC-X-2 (Blueprint line 318), AC-CS-4 (line 279), AC-CC-6 (line 281), Data Flow step 6 (line 540), Architecture Overview Banner (line 544: 'N/8 healthy'), and Verification Strategy Correctness Definition (line 1089) all uniformly codify the eight-entry inventory (7 PRD-named primaries + codebase-memory-mcp fallback). But ADR-0037 — which is the authoritative source for the mcp-events.jsonl schema bootstrap semantics — still cites seven records. The ADR is canonical; if the ADR text disagrees with the Blueprint, downstream consumers (plan-author, auditing-mcp OP-5 rule definition) face an ambiguity about the expected bootstrap-state record count.
issues.suggestion: Update ADR-0037 line 143 from 'The first postStart run appends seven readiness_probe records' to 'The first postStart run appends eight readiness_probe records (one per registered server in .mcp.json, including the codebase-memory-mcp ADR-0007 fallback per AC-X-2).' Cross-reference AC-X-2 explicitly so readers of the ADR understand why eight, not seven. This is a small text edit but should be made before Gate 4 approval so the ADR is internally consistent on first publication.

issues.description: The Sub-Agents table lists design-cicd twice (rows 2 and 9) — once for the actionlint-mcp entries, once for the Serena addition. The parenthetical at line 760 ('Serena added: mcp__serena__*; alongside the actionlint-mcp entries above') acknowledges the duplication, but the table form makes it look like a typographical defect or scanning hazard. A reader counting rows in the table might count 9 distinct agents (which is wrong — the correct count is 8 unique with design-cicd appearing twice).
issues.suggestion: Consolidate the design-cicd row to a single line listing both tool sets: '| design-cicd | mcp__actionlint-mcp__lint_workflow, mcp__actionlint-mcp__check_all_workflows, mcp__serena__* | C-0144 + ADR-0040 |'. Then the table has 8 rows for the 8 unique touched agents, matching the resolved count and removing the visual ambiguity. Also remove the resolution-note parenthetical at lines 765-766 or shorten it now that the table is self-documenting.

issues.location: Blueprint Acceptance Criteria section: AC-NFR-2-a, AC-NFR-2-c, AC-NFR-2-d are referenced (Verification Strategy line 1077-1078; State Invariants line 686; Risk Map indirectly) but the AC clauses themselves are not enumerated in the AC section of the Blueprint.
issues.description: The Blueprint AC section enumerates AC-FR-1-* through AC-FR-11-* and AC-CS-* / AC-CC-* / AC-X-1 / AC-X-2, plus AC-NFR-1-a/b for performance. But AC-NFR-2-a (no secret values committed), AC-NFR-2-c (auditing-mcp zero BLOCKER findings), and AC-NFR-2-d (runtime log redaction) — which are PRD-inherited and which several Verification Strategy bullets reference — are not present in the AC section. The Blueprint preamble at line 241 says 'inherits PRD AC-FR-* / AC-NFR-* clauses' which is the inheritance convention, but a reader auditing the Blueprint cannot read the AC-NFR-2-* text without going back to PRD v3. This is a clarity/completeness issue; the alternative (enumerate the AC-NFR-2-* clauses in the Blueprint's Cross-Layer / Operational ACs) would be self-contained.
issues.suggestion: Either (a) enumerate AC-NFR-2-a, AC-NFR-2-c, AC-NFR-2-d under 'Cross-Layer / Operational ACs' as PRD-inherited entries (mirroring how AC-NFR-1-a / AC-NFR-1-b are presently enumerated), or (b) explicitly say in the AC section preamble: 'AC-NFR-2-a, AC-NFR-2-c, AC-NFR-2-d are PRD-inherited and not re-enumerated here; see prd-v3.md §AC-NFR-2.' Option (a) is preferred for self-containment; option (b) is minimum-touch.

issues.location: ADR-0040 Decision item 2 (design-codespaces in Serena allowlist) + Blueprint Sub-Agents table row design-codespaces
issues.description: ADR-0040 includes design-codespaces in the 5-agent Serena allowlist with rationale 'may touch auditing-codespaces/scripts/ if/when the stub becomes real per ADR-0033.' But auditing-codespaces is currently STUB per ADR-0033 (per Fact Disposition row C-0499). Granting Serena access to a design agent whose target audit-script surface does not yet exist is forward-looking; if the auditing-codespaces stub is not filled in this feature's window or shortly after, design-codespaces's Serena entry sits unused. Not a blocker — additive entries are cheap — but worth surfacing as a known unknown.
issues.suggestion: Either (a) add a parenthetical to ADR-0040's design-codespaces inclusion: 'design-codespaces is included on a forward-looking basis; if the auditing-codespaces ADR-0033 stub remains unfilled for >90 days post-ship, this entry may be removed in a follow-up ADR amendment.' Or (b) document this as Known Unknown (c) under ADR-0040 Decision Details. Either makes the temporal contingency explicit. This is a recommendation, not a blocker; the inclusion itself is defensible.
